coverage_basis: A file is locked here when a production serving entry point, scripts/10_predict_slate.py or scripts/15_price_markets.py, depends on it. slate.py and storage.py are staged into the runtime bundle by the historical contract's source_files group but were never listed in its frozen_model_source_files, so their content was shipped without being pinned. Modules that merely changed during Step 3B without being on the serving path, such as ops/refresh_current_season_state.py, are deliberately not locked here.
invariant_basis: Every divergence listed above is a serving-correctness or storage determinism fix. Two of them unblock a feed that could not be produced at all: the pricing lineage tail raised KeyError, and the live Gate 3 role path failed closed on feature names the fitted model requires. The third changes only the order rows are written in. None creates or alters a probability, price, edge, EV, line or route, none changes a training feature definition, and no fitted artifact was touched. The Step 3A adaptive architecture contract remains the authority on frozen model choices and is unchanged. The fourth and fifth divergences are the real-slate serving correction: both entry points resolved the frozen manifest against the working directory, which no checkout can satisfy, so no slate could be predicted or priced at all. They add one argument and change where the same manifest is resolved, nothing else. The current relock is the live-slate feature contract: the builder emitted none of the five competition-regime flags the fitted models require, so no slate could be scored at all once the manifest did verify. It now calls the training path's own classifier instead of producing nothing, and the classifier itself is unchanged, so no feature definition moved and no rule was restated.
known_limitation: scripts/19_build_wizardofodds_runtime_bundle.py still verifies serving sources against the historical architecture reference only, so building a runtime bundle from this corrected source would fail its frozen-source check. Teaching the bundle builder about this contract is a Step 3D deployment obligation and is deliberately out of scope for this correction. Expanding this contract does not resolve that limitation.

One added import and one added keyword hand build_upcoming_slate_features the season games table, through load_history_games -- the same loader scripts/02_build_base.py and the adaptive fit already use for the same table. Without it the live builder has no schedule context and the five competition-regime flags the fitted models name in their feature lists cannot be established, so assert_model_feature_contract refuses every non-empty slate. The change is purely additive: no line the production ref has was removed or edited, every function except parse_args and main is syntax-tree-identical to production, and main's one changed statement names only the added keyword. No probability, price, edge, EV, quantile, line or routing computation was touched. || Serving-deployment correctness fix only. Both entry points verified the frozen manifest against the process working directory. The manifest records 62 files across five groups, and a Git checkout can satisfy neither the twelve ignored model binaries nor the six 2025 audit outputs, and four of its source records are already-approved divergences recorded in this contract -- so installing a verified frozen runtime bundle got the scripts past nothing and the first non-empty REFRESHED slate failed inside scripts/10_predict_slate.py at the verification, before any model was loaded. Each script gains one argument, --frozen-bundle-root, and three lines that resolve the same manifest against it when the incumbent serving caller supplies it. The change is purely additive: no line the production ref has was removed or edited, and every function except parse_args and main is syntax-tree-identical to production, which the branch-safety tests pin. No probability, price, edge, EV, quantile, line or routing computation was touched, and no manifest entry or hash was changed.

src/nba_prop_quant/slate.py.divergence_reason: Live-slate feature-contract fix. build_upcoming_slate_features assembled its row dicts from scratch and emitted none of is_regular_season, is_nba_cup, is_nba_cup_championship, is_play_in or is_playoffs. All five are named in features.FEATURE_EXACT and therefore in the fitted models' feature lists, they reached the training frame only through classify_games via build_base_frame, and assert_model_feature_contract is a column-presence check with no allowance -- so every non-empty real slate was refused after the frozen manifest had verified and no slate could be predicted or priced at all. The live builder now classifies the slate with classify_games itself, which is the single definition of those five flags, rather than with a second copy of the rules; src/nba_prop_quant/game_context.py is byte-identical to production, which the branch-safety tests pin, so the answer is still only what the classifier says. The classifier is handed the season's games table as well as the slate because Play-In detection is structural: it recognises a Play-In game by a team having already completed the season's inferred schedule length, and both the inference and the count need the season's other games. Narrowing that input to the slate's seasons is exact rather than an approximation, because classify_games infers a schedule length per season and walks each season against its own counter. Nothing is defaulted: a slate whose season carries no schedule is refused rather than scored as a regular-season game. This is a parity repair against already fitted models, not new model research: no model mathematics, model family or routing, training feature definition, marginal, copula, calibration or fitted artifact was changed, and the change is purely additive -- no line the production ref has was removed or edited, and every function in the module except build_upcoming_slate_features is syntax-tree-identical to production. || Serving-correctness fixes only, in three parts. (1) A fail-closed historical cutoff at live slate construction: build_upcoming_slate_features now refuses box-score or advanced history that is not strictly older than the slate date, before any feature is derived and therefore before all model inference. Training consumes a shifted lagged EWM state while live inference consumes the latest historical EWM state, so the two agree only under that condition. (2) Explicit NBA slate-date semantics: America/New_York is named as the canonical slate timezone for a slate date derived from an offset-aware tip timestamp, a date-only schedule field is preserved verbatim rather than reinterpreted as UTC midnight, and a naive timestamp carrying a time of day is refused rather than guessed at. (3) Live parity for player_game_number and team_game_number, which the already fitted Gate 3 role model lists in its feature_names. Both were produced only on the historical training path, so apply_gate3_role_state failed closed on the live path and assists, points+assists and points+rebounds could not be priced. The live values reproduce the existing definitions in build_base_frame exactly and are read only from history before the slate. This is a parity repair against an already fitted model, not new model research: no model mathematics, model family or routing, training feature definition, or fitted artifact was changed.
src/nba_prop_quant/slate.py.serving_role: Imported by scripts/10_predict_slate.py, which calls build_upcoming_slate_features to construct the live slate.

src/nba_prop_quant/storage.py.divergence_reason: Operational storage determinism only. upsert_parquet concatenated and deduplicated without a final sort, so the stored row order of mutable rolling state depended on the arrival order of the incoming batch and two runs over the same semantic records produced different files. Rows are now ordered by the dataset's declared key columns with a stable sort and pinned NaN placement, and the index is reset before the write. The sort runs after deduplication so keep-last still resolves a replaced record in favour of the incoming batch. No value is computed, altered or rounded: this changes the order bytes are written in, nothing else.
src/nba_prop_quant/storage.py.serving_role: Imported by scripts/10_predict_slate.py and scripts/15_price_markets.py, which call write_parquet_atomic to emit the projections and priced-markets feeds.

purpose: Pin the source that adaptive production serving actually runs. The historical static contract byte-pins nine of these files to the immutable architecture reference and remains untouched as historical evidence. This contract additionally covers serving modules the production entry points import that the historical lock never pinned, and requires every difference from the historical reference to be enumerated and justified here.
supersedes_nothing: This is additive. It does not replace, amend or reinterpret models/frozen_manifests/nba_prop_quant_v2_gate3_runtime_contract.json and it is not a new schema version of it.
